title: Understanding Oversmoothing in Diffusion-Based GNNs From the Perspective of Operator Semigroup Theory

problem.claim: The paper studies oversmoothing in diffusion-based Graph Neural Networks.

gap.claim: Prior approaches based on random walk analysis or particle systems, and prior work showing only the existence of oversmoothing, do not provide the same general theoretical characterization.

contributions.claim: The paper applies operator semigroup theory to analyze oversmoothing in diffusion-based GNNs.

It proves that oversmoothing is intrinsically linked to the ergodicity of the diffusion operator and gives a quantitative mathematical form of the smoothing feature using ergodicity and the operator's invariant measure.
It proposes a general ergodicity-breaking condition for relieving oversmoothing and provides a probabilistic interpretation connecting the theory with prior work.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their operator-semigroup approach, quantitative smoothing characterization, and more universal ergodicity-breaking condition from prior approaches and solutions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the ergodicity-breaking term mitigates oversmoothing as measured by Dirichlet energy.
The authors report that the ergodicity-breaking term improves performance on node classification tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper analyzes oversmoothing in diffusion-based GNNs.
It uses operator semigroup theory to generalize beyond random-walk and particle-system analyses.
The framework links oversmoothing to diffusion-operator ergodicity and quantitatively characterizes smoothing through ergodicity and invariant measures.
The theory yields a general ergodicity-breaking condition and a probabilistic interpretation connected to prior work.
Experiments report reduced Dirichlet-energy oversmoothing and improved node-classification performance.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal ergodicity-breaking condition.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, numerical results, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported experimental findings.
